caption: One subject's brain slice. Top: the voxels outlined in green, in the right fusiform gyrus, responded more to faces than to objects, and their signal is plotted over the scan. Bottom: a different, more medial set of voxels showed the opposite preference.
notice: The top trace rises in every face block (F) and falls in every object block (O). That tracks faces, which is a correlation; it does not by itself show the area is needed to recognise faces.

caption: Kanwisher's first look at the fusiform face area: voxels in the right fusiform gyrus (outlined in green) whose signal rose for faces and fell for objects, with the opposite pattern in a more medial region below.
notice: The signal follows the face blocks (F) up and down; imaging like this shows a correlation with faces.

caption: On the underside of the temporal lobe, part of the right fusiform gyrus (outlined in green) responded more to faces than to objects in this subject, and a more medial region did the reverse.
notice: The trace climbs in each face block (F): the ventral temporal lobe holds category-selective regions, shown here by correlation.
